_about: Declarative preference config for the run planner. Hand-authored, NOT derived.
This is the pattern the repo is meant to demonstrate: the objective function of a
planner is a product decision, so it lives in reviewable data rather than buried in
code. Changing what a run optimises for is a diff to this file.
Every selector is resolved against the real item index at build time. A selector
that matches nothing is a BUILD FAILURE, not a silent empty set -- that is what stops
an upstream rename from quietly turning a profile into a no-op.
Selector grammar, all optional, OR'd together then minus `exclude`:
patterns    case-insensitive regex over the class name
categories  whole CLE categories (tools, food, clothes, ...)
usages      items carrying that CLE usage tag

profiles.label: Base building
profiles.note: Fences, gates, watchtowers, and the tools that raise them.

profiles.label: Food & water
profiles.note: Keeping the run itself paid for.

profiles.label: Gun & gear repair
profiles.note: Keeping weapons and kit serviceable, plus ammo.

profiles.label: Hunting kit
profiles.note: What deer stands and hunting cabins actually hold.

profiles.label: Clothes to shred
profiles.note: Clothing is a rag supply: rags make bandages and rope. Value the CLE cannot see, because it is downstream of a crafting recipe rather than a property of the item.

_notes.avoidableUsages: Offered as skip toggles. A supply run into a low-tier town has no reason to route through a military base -- the risk is real and the tool cannot price it, so the player decides.
_notes.ragsource: The clearest example of why categories are not preferences: `clothes` is a CLE category, but its VALUE here comes from a crafting recipe two steps away.
